currentGrants.title: High-performance compute cluster for brain science
currentGrants.description: Funds a high-performance computing cluster for brain science research, including computational neuroscience models, deep learning experiments, and analysis of neuroimaging data.

currentGrants.title: One vision: Computational alignment of deep neural networks with humans
currentGrants.description: Develops methods to measure and improve agreement between deep neural networks and human vision. We use developmental psychology to study how visual experience shapes learning and to test training methods informed by those findings.

currentGrants.title: NSF AI Research Institute on Interaction for AI Assistants (ARIA)
currentGrants.description: Studies how AI assistants interact with people, with mental and behavioral health as a central application. Research combines computer science, cognitive neuroscience, and participatory design to study multimodal interaction, reasoning, and models of users and their environments.

currentGrants.title: Brain-inspired deep learning models of visual reasoning
currentGrants.description: Combines computational models, human psychophysics, and neurophysiology to study visual reasoning. We design tasks that expose failures in deep learning models and test whether mechanisms drawn from the brain can account for human performance.

currentGrants.title: REPRISM: Flexible embodied problem-solving by manipulating the representational prism
currentGrants.description: Studies how the representations an agent uses affect its reasoning, planning, and actions. Our contribution develops vision systems that change their representations according to the task.

currentGrants.title: SEA-CROGS: Scalable, efficient and accelerated causal reasoning operators, graphs and spikes for earth and embedded systems
currentGrants.description: Develops causal reasoning methods for Earth system science and embedded applications. The methods combine graph representations, spiking neural networks, and causal inference, with attention to computational cost.

currentGrants.title: The next generation of operator regression networks: Theory, algorithms, applications
currentGrants.description: Studies neural networks that learn mappings between function spaces. The project develops theory and algorithms for applications such as solving partial differential equations and modeling physical systems.

currentGrants.title: Enhancing suicide risk detection through computer vision
currentGrants.description: This collaboration develops computer-vision methods for clinical image analysis to support suicide-risk assessment. The work evaluates whether information extracted from images can complement clinical assessment and help improve risk detection.

currentGrants.title: A mechanistic analysis of the transition from nonsuicidal to suicidal self-injury in adolescents
currentGrants.description: This project investigates the mechanistic transition from nonsuicidal self-injury to suicidal self-injury in adolescents. Combining computational modeling with clinical assessment, the work aims to identify behavioral and cognitive markers that underlie escalation of self-injurious behavior, informing earlier and more targeted intervention.

trainingGrants.title: Brown Postdoctoral Training Program in Computational Psychiatry
trainingGrants.description: Supports postdoctoral training in computational neuroscience, machine learning, and psychiatry. Fellows learn to develop and apply computational models to questions about psychiatric disorders.

completedGrants.title: Secondary analysis of resting state MEG data using the Human Neocortical Neurosolver software tool for cellular and circuit-level interpretation
completedGrants.description: This project applied the Human Neocortical Neurosolver (HNN) software tool to resting-state magnetoencephalography (MEG) data to interpret macroscale signals in terms of their underlying cellular and circuit-level mechanisms. Our contribution focused on computational analyses linking observed oscillatory dynamics to biophysically grounded models of neocortical circuits.

completedGrants.title: Origins of Southeast Asian rainforests from paleobotany and machine learning
completedGrants.description: Developed the Virtual Paleobotany Assistant, a machine learning tool for analyzing fossil leaves and assigning them to plant families and orders. The collaboration used these analyses to study the origins of Southeast Asian tropical rainforests.

completedGrants.title: Intelligent spine interface (ISI)
completedGrants.description: Developed an interface to restore voluntary control after spinal cord injury. Our contribution used neural networks to relate stimulation patterns to motor responses.

completedGrants.title: Leveraging computer vision to augment suicide risk assessment
completedGrants.description: This project explored how computer vision could augment clinical assessment of suicide risk, in collaboration with clinical researchers.

completedGrants.title: Oscillatory processes for visual reasoning in deep neural networks
completedGrants.description: Combined biophysical models, human electrophysiology, and deep learning to study synchronized neural oscillations in visual reasoning. The project developed trainable models of oscillatory processes that could be interpreted at the neural circuit level.

completedGrants.title: Brain-inspired deep learning models of visual reasoning
completedGrants.description: Developed visual reasoning tasks and computational models to study the mechanisms underlying human performance. The work tested where deep networks fail and examined brain-inspired mechanisms for addressing those failures.

completedGrants.title: Next-generation machine vision for automated behavioral phenotyping of knock-in ALS-FTD mouse models
completedGrants.description: Developed video-based methods to measure behavior continuously in ALS-FTD mouse models, including remote video collection and cloud-based analysis.

completedGrants.title: Understanding the neural basis of the volitional state through continuous recordings in humans
completedGrants.description: Analyzed long-term intracranial recordings in humans to study how neural activity relates to voluntary action and decision-making.

completedGrants.title: Automating pathology with deep learning
completedGrants.description: Developed deep learning models to predict adverse pathology from prostate biopsies and biochemical recurrence from prostatectomy specimens. The project also examined which tissue features the models used.

completedGrants.title: Naturalistic data collection in the SmartPlayroom
completedGrants.description: Developed the SmartPlayroom to measure children’s behavior using mobile eye tracking, physiological sensors, and depth sensors. The project studied automated analysis of movement, language, eye movements, and social interactions in children aged 4–9.

completedGrants.title: WildCog: Evolution and local adaptation of cognitive abilities and brain structure in the wild
completedGrants.description: Combined measurements of fitness, cognitive performance, and neuroanatomy to study how selection shapes cognition and brain structure in wild populations.

completedGrants.title: Scaling up computational models of visual processing in cortex
completedGrants.description: Developed computational models of visual cortex that connect learnable network operations with biophysical mechanisms. The project sought simpler mathematical descriptions of those mechanisms that could be trained on visual tasks.

completedGrants.title: Computational mechanisms of rapid visual categorization: Models and psychophysics
completedGrants.description: Studied rapid visual categorization using psychophysics and models constrained by visual cortex physiology. The models were evaluated against human correct and incorrect responses and reaction times.

completedGrants.title: Development of a machine vision system for high-throughput computational behavioral analysis
completedGrants.description: Assessed customer needs and commercial uses for automated behavioral phenotyping in pharmaceutical and academic research.

completedGrants.title: Towards a biologically-inspired vision system for the control of navigation in complex environments
completedGrants.description: Developed models of vision for navigation, incorporating cortical feedforward and feedback connections, 3D shape, and motion processing. The work related model behavior to human navigation and considered applications to autonomous ground vehicles.

completedGrants.title: Development of a machine-learning and computer-vision platform for automated behavioral analysis
completedGrants.description: Developed machine learning and computer vision tools for automated measurement of animal behavior.

completedGrants.title: Towards a human-level neuromorphic artificial visual system
completedGrants.description: Studied attention and object recognition in the primate brain to develop computational models for machine vision.
